editorial:
Imagine being stuck inside a tiny apartment while the world outside is falling apart. You meet June, a former cool kid of the underground scene who now hides away in the South Bronx. It is the summer of 1977, and the city is terrified of a serial killer. The vibe is super tense because you feel June's fear growing as someone starts messing with her head. She is already struggling with her own mind, so when strange things start happening in her home, you really start to wonder what is real and what is just in her head. It feels like a pressure cooker that is about to pop.

Pam ferns does an amazing job acting as June, making you feel every bit of her panic. The way the movie tricks you is the best part, though it moves a bit slow at first. If you like mysteries that make you question everything, you will love this. For the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the gritty details of the room. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call for those crisp visuals.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that June has a split personality. The scary person tormenting her is actually another version of herself. The movie reveals that she has been fighting a war inside her own mind the whole time. In the end, she realizes the truth about her identity. It wraps up by showing that her biggest enemy was not a stranger in the Bronx, but the trauma and sickness hiding inside her own brain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and twist endings.
